name: Aeronca 65-T Defender / O-58 / L-3 Grasshopper
summary: Tiny two-seat tandem liaison and artillery-spotting airplane derived from the prewar Aeronca Defender, flown by the US Army as the O-58 and L-3 Grasshopper; the common ex-military L-3 survivors are now privately owned sport airplanes.

wings: High wing braced by a single strut on each side
Wide-chord rectangular wing with rounded tips
Fabric-covered wing with a simple, flap-free outline
engines: Single small flat-four with a two-blade fixed-pitch propeller
Plain rounded cowl with the cylinder heads showing on some examples
fuselage: Two seats in tandem under a large greenhouse with a big glazed rear window
Fixed tailwheel gear on simple spring struts
tail: Rounded fin and rudder with a gentle curve
Rounded horizontal tail, unbraced or lightly braced

tellTales: Tandem two-seater with a deep, heavily glazed greenhouse behind the wing
Tiny high-wing airplane with a rounded tail and a short, stubby cowl
Single wing strut each side with a wide-chord, rectangular wing

confusedWith.howToTell: The Champ has a lower, more cockpit-hugging cabin with a slim fuselage, while the Defender-based L-3 has a taller greenhouse that flows into a deeper rear fuselage.
The Cub has a narrow, flat-sided fuselage with a small cabin and a squared-off tail; the L-3 has a deeper, heavily glazed cabin and a rounded tail.
The L-5 is a much bigger, sleeker airplane with a six-cylinder cowl and a long sloping rear window; the L-3 is tiny with a short stubby nose.
The Taylorcraft is side-by-side with a sharply tapered rear fuselage; the L-3 seats two in tandem.
